options.counterfactual: Every normalized 2-quasitrace sends the successive differences of a bounded increasing positive sequence to zero, even when the sequence has no least upper bound.
options.approach: Seek a proof of quasitracial exhaustion using matrix amplification and the inequalities for positive elements with bounded partial sums. Such a proof would immediately imply that the required constant positive increments cannot occur.

options.approach: Investigate whether a normalized 2-quasitrace admits a state-based domination estimate strong enough to imply exhaustion. A bound of the form q(b)^p <= C phi(b) for positive contractions would rule out arbitrarily many increments of fixed quasitrace.

options.counterfactual: Every normalized 2-quasitrace sends the successive differences of a bounded increasing positive sequence to zero, even when the sequence has no least upper bound.
options.approach: Use products and ultralimits to convert exhaustion into a uniform finite packing statement. Then investigate that finite statement directly, avoiding any assumption about the existence of suprema.
